mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted as a shift toward restrictive policy, which raises the cost of capital and dampens equity valuations, thereby predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4% for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a catalyst for corporate hiring and investment, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat, and the 12-month change in PAYEMS is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) of over 0.5% for three consecutive months suggests resilient demand, which accelerates corporate investment and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth exceeds 0.5% for 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative and the 3-month PCE growth rate is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month is interpreted as a supply-side shock that reduces future earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and INDPRO recovers by less than 1% in the following month (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining CPIAUCSL inflation below 2% indicate central bank patience, which lowers policy uncertainty and tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly average < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) despite CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 suggests weakening labor demand, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and PAYEMS shows a downward trend for the following 4 months (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a decline in GDPC1 (consumer demand) creates a conflicting policy-demand tradeoff that predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 is not significant (p > 0.05) or 20-day forward returns are positive when the interaction occurs (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-recession expansion phase characterized by rising HOUST (housing starts) and UNRATE (unemployment) below 6%, S&P 500 forward returns tend to be positive over the next 5 trading days as market anticipates further economic normalization.
candidate_trigger: regime: post-recession expansion and HOUST rising while UNRATE < 6%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the identified regime conditions and HOUST growth above 2% for the following month (p < 0.05).
